minutes.headline: Commission continued most hearings and split on a Hickory Hills lake deck, which an agent check on habitat left pending.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard eleven public hearings, mostly lakefront stairs, landings and docks at Hickory Hills and Sunset Lane, plus a large warehouse proposal and a culvert replacement. It approved a field change and several negative determinations, required six replacement maples at one property, and continued several matters to May 18. A cease work order at a private property stayed in place pending review, and the agent's retirement prompted talk of applicant-funded peer review.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a plan for the Nazarenko stairs, landing and dock as submitted, over two no votes, with the agent to consult town counsel before it is signed.
A cease work order at the 430 property stays in place, with no driveway work until the commission reviews plans.
The commission continued the 160 Mass Ave culvert, 260 Fahlula Road warehouse, 379 Townsend Harbor Road and 205 Sunset Lane (Walton) dock matters.
The warehouse applicant's representative said they would consider funding a peer review during construction because the agent is retiring.
The commission approved six replacement maples at 411 Townsend Harbor Road and a field change at 398 Sunset Lane.

why_it_matters: Lakefront stairs and docks at Hickory Hills and Sunset Lane were decided here, and a resident asked whether a project could be voted without meeting priority habitat guidelines, a question the minutes do not show answered.
With the agent retiring, review of the large warehouse project may rely on an applicant-funded outside reviewer, so who pays for oversight during construction is still undecided.
watch_next: Continued hearings return on May 18, including the warehouse and culvert matters.
The commission's review of plans at the 430 property, expected in about two weeks.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most shared votes and decisions, and attendee differences are mostly name spellings. The main differences are the 411 Townsend Harbor Road vote (5-1 with a dissent officially, no dissent in ours), the 165 Townsend Harbor Road tree decision (removal in ours, replanting in the official), the Oak Ridge certificate vote that only ours records, and the five continuation votes that only the official records.
